note: Cannot confirm the BSD claim: no darwin host available here. Recording the reverse direction as evidence for the portability hazard, which does reproduce. On GNU sed 4.9 (Linux), 'sed -i s/a/b/ file' succeeds and edits in place, while the BSD-compatible form 'sed -i "" -e s/a/b/ file' fails with "sed: can't read : No such file or directory" because GNU consumes the empty string as a filename. So the incompatibility is symmetric, and a script written for either userland breaks on the other.
